input.message:
REPORT: Files tab polish + game-tour Files steps

Branch `feature/files-tab-polish`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-filestab2`, off main cc9b84a76f. One commit: `48c73ab468`. Not merged or deployed.

CHECKS
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- Full suite: 3180 tests, 46 fail. The failing names are identical to `/root/agent-notes/files-tab/v2/suite-failures-v2.txt` (diffed by name). My copy is `v3/suite-failures-v3.txt`.
- New tests, all passing:
  - `test/files-nav.test.ts`
  - `test/sftp-pool.test.ts`
  - `test/tours-files-guides.test.ts`
  - The existing `tours-trigger` and `game-files-roots` tests stay green.
- The sandbox was NOT disabled this time.
  - Every node I needed was reachable from my shell. The 4 profiled servers are on the nodes that were reachable earlier.
  - I did not try the node-5 servers, so I never hit the unreachable case.

WHAT CHANGED

1. Compact guides (`GameFilesBar.tsx`)
   - Default state is one slim strip, about 48px with padding. It scrolls sideways on a phone.
   - It shows "Where to find things", then a chip per guide (icon plus short title), a "Details" toggle, and the "Operating system files" link.
   - The one-line description is the chip's tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus, and is part of its accessible name.
   - Details expands the full cards. The choice is stored in localStorage inside try/catch and survives a reload (checked).
   - The OS banner is slim: one or two lines, the main "Open <Game> files" button, and at most 3 chips. It wraps to about 140px on a 390px screen.
   - Measured in the harness at 1440 wide, the list starts 162px below the top of the toolbar, with the strip showing and also with the banner showing.

2. Delay fix: real profile and root cause (below).

3. Click feedback
   - The pressed chip, card button, banner button, path segment or OS link shows a spinner and "Opening…", and is disabled. A second click on the same target is ignored.
   - The path bar updates at once.
   - The list area shows the NX loader, or is dimmed on a re-read.
   - An aria-live line announces "Opening /path" and then "Opened /path".
   - On failure the list area shows an inline error with Retry and "Up one folder". A missing folder says "That folder doesn't exist." there.
   - For the game controls, a missing folder shows the nearest parent plus an inline amber note.

4. Path bar (`PathBar.tsx`, new)
   - Shows the full absolute path as clickable segments, one non-wrapping row that stays scrolled to the end.
   - Has a copy button (server file sources only) and a "Game files > backups" label.
   - Checked on a deep unicode path at 390px.

5. NX preloader
   - The existing `NxLoaderMark` from `components/nx/Preloader.tsx` is reused at 56px above "Reading <path>…".
   - It shows only when a new folder has no cached listing, not on a refresh or a cached render.
   - Reduced-motion is handled by the existing CSS.

6. Tour (see below).

TIMINGS
Real running servers, read-only, directory names only, calling the actual server-side functions. These were measured before the scrypt fix; the pooled columns after it.

| Server | Per click before (median, unpooled) | After: pooled, warm | After: first call | Missing-folder fallback before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft Paper | 276 ms | 1 ms | 163 ms | 721–999 ms | 4 ms |
| Palworld | 253 ms | 1 ms | 160 ms | 672–991 ms | 4 ms |
| Project Zomboid | 195 ms | 1 ms | 149 ms | 651–739 ms | 6 ms |
| Valheim BepInEx | 241 ms | 1 ms | 156 ms | 621–1122 ms | 5 ms |

- Per-step breakdown from the first profile: DB lookup 2–30 ms, SSH+SFTP connect 155–366 ms (one run up to ~1 s), readdir 2–5 ms, close 3–6 ms.
- Warm means the server-side function only; add one browser round trip.
- After the scrypt fix the unpooled path also drops to about 165–245 ms.

ROOT CAUSE
1. Every click opened a brand-new SSH connection (TCP, key exchange, auth, SFTP subsystem). That is 97% of the time; the directory read itself is 2–5 ms.
2. Every decrypt of the root password and the management key ran `scryptSync`, about 35 ms of blocking CPU each. That is roughly 70 ms of event-loop stall per click. `lib/crypto-box.ts` now memoises the derived key per `AUTH_SECRET` value.
3. The game-folder fallback probed the landing folder and each parent one request at a time, each with its own handshake, then listed again. It is now one call, `listFilesNearest`.

CONNECTION-REUSE DESIGN (`lib/sftp-pool.ts`, wired into `lib/sftp.ts`)
- Pooled for read operations only: list and file-read.
- The pool key is `userId:serverId | host:port | credential fingerprint`.
  - Another user, another server, or a rotated password or key never gets the connection.
  - The fingerprint is a sha256 prefix, so no secret is stored in the key.
- Every action still runs session, ownership, throttle and path validation first. The pool only skips the handshake; no check is skipped.
- Idle timeout is 25 seconds; at most 32 connections, with the oldest idle evicted.
- It evicts on `close`/`end`/`error`, and on a connection-type error it retries once on a fresh connection.
- Normal SFTP errors such as "No such file" keep the connection.
- Operations on one connection are serialised; concurrent first-time connects are shared.
- It is the process's own pool (`globalThis`), not shared across users.
- Admin access gets its own admin-keyed connection.
- A security reviewer should look at this as a holding of live root SFTP connections in server memory for up to 25 seconds.

CLIENT SIDE
- Optimistic navigation.
- Per-mount stale-while-revalidate cache (`ListingCache`), keyed by source plus canonical path, cleared on every write, never a module singleton.
- Hover or focus prefetch: 150 ms rest, at most one per 400 ms, cancelled on leave.
- The new `listFilesNearest` action has the same auth, ownership, throttle and path validation as `listFiles`.

TOUR STEPS
- New `lib/tours/game-files.ts` builds two steps after `files`: `files-guides` and `files-os`. The context gets an optional `variant`, passed from `ServerTour.tsx` using `Server.gameVariant`, the same field the Files tab uses.
- Bullets come from `gameFilesFor(family, variant).guides`, at most 4, in the order: saves, add-ons, config, root folder, backups.
- Each bullet is the guide's own `<title>: <path>. <description>`. A created-later folder gets "It is created the first time you start the server or install one." Backups get "It is created with your first backup."
- Anchors added:
  - `files-guides`: on all three bar states, so it works with Details open or closed.
  - `files-pathbar`: on the path bar.
  - `files-os-link`: on the OS link, only while browsing inside the game's area.
- A grep-level test checks the anchors exist. `docs/TOURS.md` documents the steps and the anchors, and says a new game gets this automatically from `lib/game-files-roots.ts`.
- `files-guides` is NOT `optional`. In this engine `optional: true` skips the step when the anchor is missing. A stopped server has no file manager, so I kept the centred-card fallback.
- Vanilla nudge: when a type has no add-on folder but another selectable type of the same game does, one extra sentence names those Settings server types. It uses only the types the Settings picker lists, so Rust Carbon is excluded. Settings does list Paper/Purpur/Fabric/Forge for Minecraft and BepInEx for Valheim.
- The tests loop over every family and every variant: the tour builds, ids are unique, the steps are serialisable, there are 1–4 bullets, each maps to a real guide or the root folder, and there is no "provider" or "one-click" wording.

Step text, as rendered by the real tour engine:
- minecraft paper: "Your Minecraft files are one click away: the shortcuts here jump straight to the right folder." Bullets:
  - "World saves: /opt/mc/world. Download your world or upload a replacement here. Stop the server before replacing saves."
  - "Plugins: /opt/mc/plugins. Upload plugin .jar files here, then restart the server. It is created the first time you start the server or install one."
  - "Server settings: /opt/mc. server.properties and the other settings files are in the main folder."
  - "Your backups: /var/backups/nxeon-game. Backups you make with Back up now are saved here as .tar.gz files. It is created with your first backup."
- minecraft fabric: same intro. Bullets: World saves; "Mods: /opt/mc/mods. Upload mod .jar files here, then restart the server. It is created the first time you start the server or install one."; Server settings; Your backups.
- minecraft vanilla: intro plus "Your server type doesn't use plugins or mods; the Paper, Purpur, Fabric or Forge server type in Settings does." Bullets: World saves; Server settings; Your backups (no Plugins or Mods).
- valheim bepinex: "Your Valheim files are one click away: …" Bullets:
  - "World saves: /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local. …"
  - "Mods (BepInEx): /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins. Upload BepInEx mod .dll files here, then restart the server."
  - "Game folder: /opt/valheim/config. The main folder for your server's files."
  - "Backups: /opt/valheim/config/backups. The server keeps automatic world backups here."
- palworld (generated by the same code; not captured from the engine): World saves `/opt/palworld/Pal/Saved/SaveGames`; Config files `/opt/palworld/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer`; "Game folder: /opt/palworld. The main folder for your server's files."; Backups `/opt/palworld/backups`. No mods bullet, and no nudge.
- terraria: "World and settings: /opt/terraria. Your world (.wld files) and the TShock settings are in this folder. Stop the server before replacing saves."; "TShock plugins: /opt/terraria-plugins. … It is created the first time you start the server or install one."; "Backups: /opt/terraria/backups. TShock's world backups are saved here."
- sonsoftheforest (script-derived, saves plus settings only): "Saves and settings: /opt/sonsoftheforest/userdata. Your saves and dedicatedserver.cfg are in this folder. Stop the server before replacing saves."; "Game folder: /opt/sonsoftheforest. The main folder for your server's files."; "Your backups: /var/backups/nxeon-game. … It is created with your first backup."
- files-os (all games): "Going up to / shows the server's own operating system files; an amber warning appears there, and “Open <Game> files” brings you back. The path bar always shows exactly where you are, with a copy button."

SCREENSHOTS
- `/root/agent-notes/files-tab/v3/` (1440 and 390 wide):
  - landing with the compact strip, and the Details-expanded state;
  - the slim OS banner;
  - chip tooltip on hover;
  - click feedback with the NX preloader above "Reading /opt/terraria/backups…";
  - the state after opening;
  - a deep unicode path bar;
  - the missing-folder fallback;

- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- Full suite: 3180 tests, 46 fail. The failing names are identical to `/root/agent-notes/files-tab/v2/suite-failures-v2.txt` (diffed by name). My copy is `v3/suite-failures-v3.txt`.

  - `test/sftp-pool.test.ts`
  - `test/tours-files-guides.test.ts`
  - The existing `tours-trigger` and `game-files-roots` tests stay green.
- The sandbox was NOT disabled this time.
  - Every node I needed was reachable from my shell. The 4 profiled servers are on the nodes that were reachable earlier.
  - I did not try the node-5 servers, so I never hit the unreachable case.

WHAT CHANGED

1. Compact guides (`GameFilesBar.tsx`)
   - Default state is one slim strip, about 48px with padding. It scrolls sideways on a phone.
   - It shows "Where to find things", then a chip per guide (icon plus short title), a "Details" toggle, and the "Operating system files" link.
   - The one-line description is the chip's tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus, and is part of its accessible name.
   - Details expands the full cards. The choice is stored in localStorage inside try/catch and survives a reload (checked).
   - The OS banner is slim: one or two lines, the main "Open <Game> files" button, and at most 3 chips. It wraps to about 140px on a 390px screen.
   - Measured in the harness at 1440 wide, the list starts 162px below the top of the toolbar, with the strip showing and also with the banner showing.

2. Delay fix: real profile and root cause (below).

3. Click feedback
   - The pressed chip, card button, banner button, path segment or OS link shows a spinner and "Opening…", and is disabled. A second click on the same target is ignored.
   - The path bar updates at once.
   - The list area shows the NX loader, or is dimmed on a re-read.
   - An aria-live line announces "Opening /path" and then "Opened /path".
   - On failure the list area shows an inline error with Retry and "Up one folder". A missing folder says "That folder doesn't exist." there.
   - For the game controls, a missing folder shows the nearest parent plus an inline amber note.

4. Path bar (`PathBar.tsx`, new)
   - Shows the full absolute path as clickable segments, one non-wrapping row that stays scrolled to the end.
   - Has a copy button (server file sources only) and a "Game files > backups" label.
   - Checked on a deep unicode path at 390px.

5. NX preloader
   - The existing `NxLoaderMark` from `components/nx/Preloader.tsx` is reused at 56px above "Reading <path>…".
   - It shows only when a new folder has no cached listing, not on a refresh or a cached render.
   - Reduced-motion is handled by the existing CSS.

6. Tour (see below).

TIMINGS
Real running servers, read-only, directory names only, calling the actual server-side functions. These were measured before the scrypt fix; the pooled columns after it.

| Server | Per click before (median, unpooled) | After: pooled, warm | After: first call | Missing-folder fallback before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft Paper | 276 ms | 1 ms | 163 ms | 721–999 ms | 4 ms |
| Palworld | 253 ms | 1 ms | 160 ms | 672–991 ms | 4 ms |
| Project Zomboid | 195 ms | 1 ms | 149 ms | 651–739 ms | 6 ms |
| Valheim BepInEx | 241 ms | 1 ms | 156 ms | 621–1122 ms | 5 ms |

- Per-step breakdown from the first profile: DB lookup 2–30 ms, SSH+SFTP connect 155–366 ms (one run up to ~1 s), readdir 2–5 ms, close 3–6 ms.
- Warm means the server-side function only; add one browser round trip.
- After the scrypt fix the unpooled path also drops to about 165–245 ms.

ROOT CAUSE
1. Every click opened a brand-new SSH connection (TCP, key exchange, auth, SFTP subsystem). That is 97% of the time; the directory read itself is 2–5 ms.
2. Every decrypt of the root password and the management key ran `scryptSync`, about 35 ms of blocking CPU each. That is roughly 70 ms of event-loop stall per click. `lib/crypto-box.ts` now memoises the derived key per `AUTH_SECRET` value.
3. The game-folder fallback probed the landing folder and each parent one request at a time, each with its own handshake, then listed again. It is now one call, `listFilesNearest`.

CONNECTION-REUSE DESIGN (`lib/sftp-pool.ts`, wired into `lib/sftp.ts`)
- Pooled for read operations only: list and file-read.
- The pool key is `userId:serverId | host:port | credential fingerprint`.
  - Another user, another server, or a rotated password or key never gets the connection.
  - The fingerprint is a sha256 prefix, so no secret is stored in the key.
- Every action still runs session, ownership, throttle and path validation first. The pool only skips the handshake; no check is skipped.
- Idle timeout is 25 seconds; at most 32 connections, with the oldest idle evicted.
- It evicts on `close`/`end`/`error`, and on a connection-type error it retries once on a fresh connection.
- Normal SFTP errors such as "No such file" keep the connection.
- Operations on one connection are serialised; concurrent first-time connects are shared.
- It is the process's own pool (`globalThis`), not shared across users.
- Admin access gets its own admin-keyed connection.
- A security reviewer should look at this as a holding of live root SFTP connections in server memory for up to 25 seconds.

CLIENT SIDE
- Optimistic navigation.
- Per-mount stale-while-revalidate cache (`ListingCache`), keyed by source plus canonical path, cleared on every write, never a module singleton.
- Hover or focus prefetch: 150 ms rest, at most one per 400 ms, cancelled on leave.
- The new `listFilesNearest` action has the same auth, ownership, throttle and path validation as `listFiles`.

TOUR STEPS
- New `lib/tours/game-files.ts` builds two steps after `files`: `files-guides` and `files-os`. The context gets an optional `variant`, passed from `ServerTour.tsx` using `Server.gameVariant`, the same field the Files tab uses.
- Bullets come from `gameFilesFor(family, variant).guides`, at most 4, in the order: saves, add-ons, config, root folder, backups.
- Each bullet is the guide's own `<title>: <path>. <description>`. A created-later folder gets "It is created the first time you start the server or install one." Backups get "It is created with your first backup."
- Anchors added:
  - `files-guides`: on all three bar states, so it works with Details open or closed.
  - `files-pathbar`: on the path bar.
  - `files-os-link`: on the OS link, only while browsing inside the game's area.
- A grep-level test checks the anchors exist. `docs/TOURS.md` documents the steps and the anchors, and says a new game gets this automatically from `lib/game-files-roots.ts`.
- `files-guides` is NOT `optional`. In this engine `optional: true` skips the step when the anchor is missing. A stopped server has no file manager, so I kept the centred-card fallback.
- Vanilla nudge: when a type has no add-on folder but another selectable type of the same game does, one extra sentence names those Settings server types. It uses only the types the Settings picker lists, so Rust Carbon is excluded. Settings does list Paper/Purpur/Fabric/Forge for Minecraft and BepInEx for Valheim.
- The tests loop over every family and every variant: the tour builds, ids are unique, the steps are serialisable, there are 1–4 bullets, each maps to a real guide or the root folder, and there is no "provider" or "one-click" wording.

content.text:
I've finished both parts on `feature/files-tab-polish` (commit `48c73ab468`): the Files tab polish and the new game-tour steps. Nothing is merged or deployed, and I didn't disable the sandbox this time.

`tsc` is clean and the new tests pass. The full suite has 46 failures, with the same names as `v2/suite-failures-v2.txt`. I checked the UI only on a throwaway harness (the real file browser and the real tour engine over a fake in-memory server), not on the real `/dashboard/servers/[id]` page, which needs a session and a live server. I also never ran the pooled reads through the real Next server actions; I timed the server-side functions directly against real servers.

**Cause of the delay:** every folder click opened a fresh SSH connection (150–350 ms), and each decrypt of the root password and management key ran a blocking `scryptSync` on top (about 35 ms each). The directory read itself takes 2–5 ms. The game-folder fallback made it worse by probing parents one at a time, each with its own handshake.

**Fixes:**
- **Pool:** a short-lived SSH connection pool for list and file-read only.
  - The key includes user id, server id, target and a credential fingerprint.
  - Connections idle out after 25 seconds and are capped at 32.
  - Every call still runs the session, ownership, throttle and path checks first.
  - It does hold live root SFTP connections in server memory for up to 25 seconds, which a security reviewer should look at.
- **`scryptSync`:** the derived key is memoised in `lib/crypto-box.ts`.
- **Fallback:** the missing-folder fallback is now a single call.
- **Client:** navigation is optimistic, with a per-mount stale-while-revalidate cache, a hover prefetch and a double-click guard.

Measured on four real running servers (read-only):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Per folder click | ~195–276 ms | ~1 ms warm, ~150–165 ms on first connect |
| Missing-folder fallback | ~620–1120 ms | 4–6 ms |

Warm means the server-side function only, so add one browser round trip. The "before" column is from before the `scryptSync` fix.

**UI changes:**
- **Strip:** the guides are now one slim strip of chips, with the description as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. A Details toggle expands the cards, and the choice survives a reload.
- **Banner:** the OS banner is slim.
- **List position:** in the harness at 1440 wide, the file list starts 162 px below the top of the toolbar, with the strip showing and with the banner showing.
- **Feedback:** the pressed control shows a spinner and "Opening…" and is disabled, and a screen-reader line announces the folder. Failures show an inline error with Retry.
- **Path bar:** a new path bar shows the full path with a copy button and a "Game files > backups" label.
- **Preloader:** the existing NX loader appears above "Reading <path>…" when a new folder opens.

**Tour:** two new steps follow `files`, `files-guides` and `files-os`. The bullets come from the same guide data the Files tab uses, filtered by the server's `gameVariant` and capped at four. Folders created later say so. A Vanilla server gets one extra sentence pointing to the server types in Settings, naming only types the picker offers. Anchors `files-guides`, `files-pathbar` and `files-os-link` are in place.

Questions for you:
- **Missing anchor:** the `files-guides` step is not marked `optional`, because `optional` skips the step when its anchor is missing in this engine. Without it, a stopped server (no file manager) still shows the step as a centred card. Do you want it skipped instead?
- **Vanilla wording:** the Vanilla sentence assumes switching the server type in Settings on an existing server works. The picker is there and the existing tour already says so, but I didn't verify that a switch installs the right jar.

The full report has the step text for Minecraft Paper, Fabric and Vanilla, Valheim BepInEx, Terraria, Sons of the Forest and Palworld. The Palworld text is generated by the same code but wasn't captured from the engine.

Screenshots at 1440 and 390 are in `/root/agent-notes/files-tab/v3/` (tour steps in `v3/tour/`), with the harness scripts in `v3/harness/`.
